newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut bank shares down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Beirut bank shares down on profit-taking.

text.p: The star shares on the Beirut Stock Exchange, Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce and Banque Audi, fell slightly on Monday as investors took profits after nearly five months of steady upward movement.
BLC fell to $17 from $17.25 and Banque Audi went down to $20 from $20.125. They were the shares' first declines since listing last December and January at $11.25 and $15 respectively.
The third listed bank, Bank of Beirut, was unchanged at $3.5625.
The LIBX bank index fell 0.69 percent to 138.78 and the LISPI and BLOM general indices fell 0.66 percent and 1.27 percent to 87.79 and 995.15 respectively.
"This is normal profit-taking by some investors," a broker told Reuters.
"The market was very quiet, the banks' fall is not a trend. It is an adjustment after a continuous rise since they were listed," another broker said.
Solidere B shares fell to $11.75 from $12.25 following a surge last week while A shares held steady at $11.5. There was no demand for A shares at the second fixing.
Total BSE turnover fell to 203,310 shares for a value of $1,954,167 from 335,408 shares and $4,522,119 on Friday.
"We have not seen such a boring day on the market for nearly two months. The market was very quiet," Tania Hajj, a broker for Arab Finance Corporation, told Reuters.
Among the four industrial companies 10,000 Ciments Libanaise shares and 12,000 shares of pipemaker Eternit were traded unchanged at $1.2812 and $1.875 respectively.
There was no trade in Ciments Blancs and Uniceramic.
